Define a Risk Scoring Model

Source: R/risk_models.R
risk_model.Rd

Wraps a scoring rule so the engine can score risks with something other than the default FMEA product. A model turns a data.frame of risks into a raw score, a normalized 0–100 risk score, and a qualitative level. Use the pre-built models or supply your own score function.

Usage

risk_model(name, score, max_raw, bands, required = character())

Arguments

name

A short model name.

score

A function taking a data.frame of risks and returning a numeric vector of raw scores, one per row.

max_raw

The raw score at maximum risk, used to normalize to 0–100.

bands

A named list of c(lower, upper) boundaries over the raw score, ordered from highest risk to lowest. Evaluated in order; first match wins.

required

Character vector of columns the score function needs.

Value

An object of class "risk_model".

Examples

risks <- data.frame(
  risk_id     = c("R001", "R002", "R003"),
  probability = c(4, 3, 2),
  impact      = c(5, 4, 3),
  detectability = c(2, 3, 4)
)
m <- risk_model(
  name = "impact_only",
  score = function(df) df$impact,
  max_raw = 5,
  bands = list(high = c(4, 5), medium = c(3, 3), low = c(1, 2)),
  required = "impact"
)
apply_risk_model(risks, m)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   risk_id raw_score risk_score risk_level model      
#>   <chr>       <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>      <chr>      
#> 1 R001            5        100 high       impact_only
#> 2 R002            4         80 high       impact_only
#> 3 R003            3         60 medium     impact_only
